summary: gs-rest-service: druntime's default GC pools against minPoolSize:1 incPoolSize:0 parallel:1, same binary, Go interleaved, 4 trials
why: Decision-gating A/B (coordinator, 2026-11-23); run after gs-rest-multicore-5. The same Flint binary at b481428a005a runs under --DRT-gcopt='gc:conservative profile:1' (druntime's default) and --DRT-gcopt='gc:conservative minPoolSize:1 incPoolSize:0 parallel:1 profile:1', with the registered Go comparator, interleaved in every trial (Go, A, B, then B, A, Go), on the workload of policy/spring-http-benchmark.json with 4 trials instead of 9 so it fits a claimed window. Reports peak RSS, throughput, p50, p99, CPU per request and druntime's collections and pauses per arm. Decision: if small-pools lowers peak RSS and costs no other metric beyond its interval, Boot bakes it into rt_options with a playbook entry; if it costs p99 or throughput, minPoolSize:2 and 4 are next. The record is mode "ab" and never counts as the Phase 1 GC matrix. Agreed with proof-harness (2026-11-23 21:15Z): priority 2, so it runs right after gs-rest-multicore-5 (priority 1) and ahead of build runs; proof-harness adds small-pools/default ratios of medians with bootstrap 99% intervals from the raw series, wide at 4 trials per arm, so 'no metric worse beyond its interval' is a lenient test and the result says so.
